 Basel SF previews and predictions: Fritz vs. Vacherot, Lehecka vs. Struff 
 October 30, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Match previews 
 5 
 It is a relatively surprising semifinal lineup in Basel, where No. 6 Taylor Fritz is the highest seed remaining and will continue his title quest against Valentin Vacherot on Saturday. No. 8 Jiri Lehecka runs into a red-hot Jan-Lennard Struff. 
 Valentin Vacherot vs. (6) Taylor Fritz
Fritz and Struff will be facing each other for the second time in their careers and for the second time at the Swiss Indoors Basel when they meet again on semifinal Saturday. They collided in the first round 12 months ago, when Fritz survived a 4-6, 7-6(4), 7-5 thriller. It has been an ideal week so far for the 13th-ranked American, who is suddenly in very realistic Nitto ATP Finals contention following wins over Rinky Hijikata, Denis Shapovalov, and Arthur Fils. Meanwhile, fellow Turin contenders Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe, Rafael Jodar, and Novak Djokovic have already exited their respective tournaments.
Vacherot, who has also dealt with some physical issues in 2026, is coming down the stretch of a solid but unspectacular year. The 31st-ranked Monegasque was a semifinalist in Tokyo earlier this month and has battled into the last four this week thanks to defeats of Mariano Navone, Rafael Jodar (in a third-set tiebreaker), and Holger Rune. Coming off two very difficult matches and now facing an in-form and motivated opponent, this could be the end of the road for Vacherot.
 Pick: Fritz in 2

 (8) Jiri Lehecka vs. (SE) Jan-Lennard Struff
At 36 years old, Struff is playing close to the best tennis of his career. The 47th-ranked German advanced to the Wimbledon quarterfinals, finished runner-up last week in Brussels, and has made a run to the Basel semis at the expense of Yannick Hanfmann, Djokovic, and Nuno Borges. In between two blowouts of Hanfmann and Borges, Struff upset Djokovic 6-7(4), 7-5, 7-6(5) on Thursday.
Standing in Struff’s way of another title match is Lehecka, who leads the head-to-head series 3-0. However, they have never squared off indoors — never on any kind of hard court, in fact. Lehecka is also in strong form, with a runner-up effort in Tokyo, a quarterfinal result in Brussels, and Basel victories over Stan Wawrinka, Daniel Altmaier, and Jerome Kym. The 21st-ranked Czech may be the favorite, but this is a dangerous matchup for him — as it would be for anyone. Struff has dropped serve only twice through three rounds in Basel, including not a single time in three long sets against Djokovic.
 Pick: Struff in 3
